40: class ProtocolRunner(TypingProtocol):
41:     """An interface to manage and control a protocol run.
42: 
43:     The ProtocolRunner is primarily responsible for feeding a ProtocolEngine
44:     with commands and control signals. These commands and signals are
45:     generated by protocol files, hardware signals, or externally via
46:     the HTTP robot-server.
47: 
48:     A ProtocolRunner controls a single run. Once the run is finished,
49:     you will need a new ProtocolRunner to do another run.
50:     """
51: 
52:     def was_started(self) -> bool:
53:         """Whether the runner has been started.
54: 
55:         This value is latched; once it is True, it will never become False.
56:         """
57: 
58:     async def load(self, protocol_source: ProtocolSource) -> None:
59:         """Load a ProtocolSource into managed ProtocolEngine.
60: 
61:         Calling this method is only necessary if the runner will be used
62:         to control the run of a file-based protocol.
63:         """
64: 
65:     def play(self) -> None:
66:         """Start or resume the run."""
67: 
68:     def pause(self) -> None:
69:         """Pause the run."""
70: 
71:     async def stop(self) -> None:
72:         """Stop (cancel) the run."""
73: 
74:     async def run(
75:         self,
76:         protocol_source: Optional[ProtocolSource] = None,
77:     ) -> ProtocolRunResult:
78:         """Run a given protocol to completion."""
